speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I need to assess your newborn's increasing yellow discoloration. When did you first notice the jaundice, and is the baby feeding well and producing normal wet diapers?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-week-old female newborn. The patient has been experiencing increasing yellow discoloration of her eyes and skin for 2 days. She was born at 39 weeks' gestation, initially weighed 3066 g and now weighs 3200 g. The patient is exclusively breastfed.

speaker: Doctor
text: It is good to hear the baby is gaining weight and feeding exclusively. I would like to check her stool and urine color; are the stools yellow and the urine clear, or have you noticed pale, clay-colored stools or dark urine?

text:
My main symptom is Increasing yellow discoloration of the eyes and skin. I also have Exclusively breastfed, Brother died 3 months after liver surgery.

speaker: Doctor
text: The family history of a brother dying after liver surgery is a significant red flag for a genetic metabolic disorder like Tyrosinemia Type 1, rather than simple breast milk jaundice. REQUEST TEST: Serum_total_and_direct_bilirubin, Liver_function_tests, Urine_tyrosine

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Bilirubin_Total: 16.1 mg/dL, Bilirubin_Direct: 0.7 mg/dL, Alkaline_Phosphatase: 22 U/L, AST: 12 U/L, ALT: 12 U/L

speaker: Doctor
text: The test results show predominantly unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia with normal liver enzymes, which makes Tyrosinemia Type 1 unlikely given the lack of liver dysfunction. I will now check for signs of hemolysis by requesting a Coombs test and a complete blood count to rule out blood group incompatibility or other hematologic causes. REQUEST TEST: Direct_Coombs_test, Complete_Blood_Count

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Direct Coombs test: Negative, Hematocrit: 51%

speaker: Doctor
text: The negative Coombs test and normal hematocrit rule out hemolytic disease, while the normal liver enzymes and unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia in a thriving, exclusively breastfed infant strongly point to breast milk jaundice. DIAGNOSIS READY: Breast milk jaundice
